denial.text: Prairie Commons Medicaid Plan denied the claim for CPT 35301 (carotid endarterectomy) with date of service 2026-08-07. CARC 167: This (these) diagnosis(es) is (are) not covered. Payer remark: The diagnosis reported (cerebral atherosclerosis, unspecified) is not a covered indication for this procedure.

criteria.text: Symptomatic carotid stenosis: transient ischemic attack, amaurosis fugax, or non-disabling stroke in the ipsilateral territory within the past 6 months with 50 to 99 percent stenosis; or asymptomatic 70 to 99 percent stenosis with a life expectancy over 5 years and a perioperative stroke and death risk under 3 percent.
Degree of stenosis documented by duplex ultrasound using velocity criteria, confirmed by CT or MR angiography when indicated, reported by the NASCET method.
Best medical therapy in place: antiplatelet therapy and a high-intensity statin.
Surgery planned within 14 days of the index event when feasible.

chart.text: Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.
Vitamin D came back 15. Started 1000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.
From the referring physician: please evaluate and treat as you see fit. We have exhausted what we can do in primary care and the patient is motivated. Recent labs enclosed, all within normal limits.
Work note requested for a sick day last Monday. Faxed to the employer.

Called his with the cholesterol results. Total 233, LDL 117, HDL 62, triglycerides 192. Discussed diet and walking. He wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.

Here with a cough and congestion for 6 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if he gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.

Mole on the upper back that his spouse noticed. About 6 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change he is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.
Twenty minutes of left arm weakness and slurred speech that resolved before arrival. CT head without hemorrhage or infarct. ABCD2 score 5. Aspirin given, carotid imaging ordered, neurology consulted.

Carotid duplex. Right internal carotid peak systolic velocity 310 centimeters per second, end diastolic velocity 125, ICA to CCA ratio 4.4, consistent with 70 to 99 percent stenosis. Left 1 to 39 percent.
CT angiography of the neck: right internal carotid artery 81 percent stenosis by NASCET criteria with an ulcerated, partly calcified plaque at the bulb. Left 30 percent. Intracranial vessels patent.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 20. Approved 90 days. He mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.
Dermatology consult note received. Two actinic keratoses on the forehead treated with cryotherapy. Annual skin check recommended, sunscreen counseling done.

69 year old man in vascular surgery clinic after a recent neurologic event, sent by neurology. Significant plaque on the right. Hypertension, hyperlipidemia, type 2 diabetes. Discussed endarterectomy versus stenting; endarterectomy preferred for this anatomy and age. His history otherwise: hypothyroidism on levothyroxine, hypertension on lisinopril. Allergies: no drug allergies. Quit smoking 12 years ago, no alcohol, works two jobs. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. Transient ischemic attack 11 days ago, left arm and face, now back to baseline. Symptomatic right carotid disease. Aspirin 81 and clopidogrel 75 started in the emergency department, atorvastatin 80 nightly, blood pressure 138 over 82 today. Scheduling endarterectomy within 2 weeks of the event per guideline; the operating room is booked for 13 days from today.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 14 and 18. No ocular pathology noted.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, he will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.

Returned with his daughter to go over the operation, the risk of stroke with and without surgery, cranial nerve injury, and the hospital stay of one night. Wants to proceed. Vitals today 130 over 76, pulse 64.
Patient called about a tick bite on the scalp after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.
He called asking about travel vaccines for a trip in the spring. Advised hepatitis A and a typhoid booster, referred to the travel clinic. Nothing else needed from us.
Pre-op. Anesthesia evaluation done, EKG unchanged. Continue aspirin and clopidogrel through surgery. Consent signed.

expected.note: The chart documents every criterion; the CARC 167 denial can be answered from the record.
